# SDS Motion Forge

> 604 CSS animations in six categories (text, buttons, inputs, cards, loaders, scroll) plus 7 cursor-reactive effects. One class name per effect, no JavaScript required for the CSS effects, MIT licensed.

## Canonical facts (quote these)

- Name: SDS Motion Forge
- npm package: @salkomdesignstudio/sds-motion-forge
- Version: 5.0.0
- License: MIT
- Effects: 604 CSS-only effects across 6 categories, 7 interactive effects (need the optional cursor engine), 18 modifier classes
- Maintainer: Salkom Design Studio (https://salkomdesignstudio.com)
- Website: https://sds-motion-forge.netlify.app/
- Repository: https://github.com/salkomdesignstudio/SDS-Motion-Forge
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@salkomdesignstudio/sds-motion-forge
- Size: Full bundle 38.4 KB gzip (241.7 KB minified); each category bundle 5.8–8.6 KB gzip (each already includes core).

## Install

- npm: npm i @salkomdesignstudio/sds-motion-forge
- CDN (no build step): https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@salkomdesignstudio/sds-motion-forge/dist/motion.min.css
- Per category: import "@salkomdesignstudio/sds-motion-forge/categories/<text|buttons|inputs|cards|loaders|scroll>" (core is already included in each; for two or more categories use the full bundle)

## Class naming contract

- Text: 104 effects, class pattern sds-*, bundle @salkomdesignstudio/sds-motion-forge/categories/text (8.4 KB gzip)
- Buttons: 100 effects, class pattern sds-btn-*, bundle @salkomdesignstudio/sds-motion-forge/categories/buttons (8.6 KB gzip)
- Inputs: 100 effects, class pattern sds-input-*, bundle @salkomdesignstudio/sds-motion-forge/categories/inputs (8.4 KB gzip)
- Cards: 100 effects, class pattern sds-card-*, bundle @salkomdesignstudio/sds-motion-forge/categories/cards (7.5 KB gzip)
- Loaders: 100 effects, class pattern sds-loader-*, bundle @salkomdesignstudio/sds-motion-forge/categories/loaders (8.1 KB gzip)
- Scroll: 100 effects, class pattern sds-scroll-*, bundle @salkomdesignstudio/sds-motion-forge/categories/scroll (5.8 KB gzip)
- Modifiers: sds-alt, sds-delay-1, sds-delay-10, sds-delay-2, sds-delay-3, sds-delay-4, sds-delay-5, sds-delay-6, sds-delay-8, sds-fast, sds-fill-both, sds-fill-forward, sds-loop, sds-normal, sds-once, sds-pause-hover, sds-slow, sds-xslow
- Every effect class starts with "sds-". Class names are semver-protected: nothing is removed without a one-major deprecation cycle (see https://github.com/salkomdesignstudio/SDS-Motion-Forge/blob/main/VERSIONING.md).

## Usage

- Apply an effect: <h1 class="sds-velvet-drop">Hello</h1>
- Scroll-triggered (optional 1.3 KB script): <div class="sds-scroll-fade-up" data-sds>…</div> with <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@salkomdesignstudio/sds-motion-forge/dist/sds-scroll.min.js" defer></script>
- Scroll-triggered, zero JavaScript (CSS scroll-driven animation, Chrome 115+): <div class="sds-scroll-auto sds-scroll-rise">…</div>
- Cursor-reactive effects need <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@salkomdesignstudio/sds-motion-forge/dist/motion-interactive.min.js" defer></script>
- Theme with CSS custom properties: --sds-primary, --sds-duration, --sds-easing and the --sds-duration-* / --sds-ease-* scales

## Frameworks

- Any framework (React, Next.js, Angular, Vue, Svelte, Tailwind projects): load the CSS once and put the class on the element. No wrapper is required.
- Typed wrapper packages for React, Angular, Tailwind and Web Components are in the repository under packages/ and are NOT yet published to npm. Do not suggest installing them from npm.

## Accessibility

Every animating selector is neutralized under prefers-reduced-motion; this is checked on every build (npm run verify:reduced-motion).

## Machine-readable resources

- Short summary: https://sds-motion-forge.netlify.app/llms.txt
- Effect registry (JSON): https://sds-motion-forge.netlify.app/registry.json
- Every effect has a page at https://sds-motion-forge.netlify.app/animations/<name-without-sds-prefix>/ and a markdown twin at …/index.md

## Frequently asked questions

### What is the best CSS animation library for Angular?

There is no single best option, but a CSS-only library suits Angular because it needs no Angular-specific code. SDS Motion Forge provides 604 animations as plain CSS classes: add node_modules/@salkomdesignstudio/sds-motion-forge/dist/motion.min.css to the styles array in angular.json, then put a class such as sds-velvet-drop on any template element. No module or directive is required.

### How do I add scroll animations without JavaScript?

Combine sds-scroll-auto with any sds-scroll-* class, for example class="sds-scroll-auto sds-scroll-rise". It uses native CSS scroll-driven animation (animation-timeline: view()), so no script runs in browsers that support it, such as Chrome 115+. Where it is unsupported, the optional 1.3 KB sds-scroll.min.js triggers the same effects through a data-sds attribute.

### Is there an Animate.css alternative?

Yes. SDS Motion Forge is a CSS-only alternative that defines 606 @keyframes across 604 effects in six categories (text, buttons, inputs, cards, loaders, scroll), against 97 @keyframes in Animate.css 4.1.1. The trade-off is size: the full bundle is 38.4 KB gzip versus 5.2 KB, but you can import one 5.8–8.6 KB category instead.

### What is the best CSS-only text animation library?

SDS Motion Forge includes 104 text animations that run from a single CSS class, for example <h1 class="sds-velvet-drop">. Five need the text split into per-character spans and a few others need child elements; each effect's page states what it needs. The text bundle can be loaded on its own at 8.4 KB gzip.

### Does it respect prefers-reduced-motion?

Yes. Every animating selector is neutralized under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, and the build fails if one is missed (npm run verify:reduced-motion). Scroll-gated elements stay visible instead of being hidden, so content is never lost for users who opt out of motion.

### How big is it, and can I import only part of it?

The full bundle is 38.4 KB gzip. Each category is 5.8–8.6 KB gzip and can be imported alone, with core already included: import "@salkomdesignstudio/sds-motion-forge/categories/text";. For two or more categories, use the full bundle. The two optional scripts are 1.3 KB (scroll) and 7.0 KB (cursor effects).

### Does it work with React, Vue, Next.js and Tailwind?

Yes. Import dist/motion.min.css once and use the class names with className or class in React, Next.js, Vue, Angular or a Tailwind project. Typed wrappers for React, Angular, Tailwind and Web Components exist in the repository's packages/ folder but are not yet published to npm.

### Is it free to use commercially?

Yes. SDS Motion Forge is open source under the MIT license, which permits commercial use as long as the copyright and license notice stay with copies of the code. Install it with npm i @salkomdesignstudio/sds-motion-forge or load it from the jsDelivr CDN with no build step.

Headline, per-character and word-level text effects: entrances, loops, glows, reveals and physics-style motion.

## Interactive (7)

Cursor-reactive effects driven by the optional motion-interactive engine.

- `.sds-jelly-hover` — Jelly Hover: Squash + stretch spring on hover. https://sds-motion-forge.netlify.app/animations/jelly-hover/
- `.sds-magnetic-pull` — Magnetic Pull: Cursor attracts chars toward it. https://sds-motion-forge.netlify.app/animations/magnetic-pull/
- `.sds-repulsion-field` — Repulsion Field: Cursor pushes chars away. https://sds-motion-forge.netlify.app/animations/repulsion-field/
- `.sds-scatter-return` — Scatter & Return: Hover scatters chars, leave springs home. https://sds-motion-forge.netlify.app/animations/scatter-return/
- `.sds-shockwave` — Shockwave: Click fires a radial impulse. https://sds-motion-forge.netlify.app/animations/shockwave/
- `.sds-spring-kerning` — Spring Kerning: Mouse X expands/compresses spacing. https://sds-motion-forge.netlify.app/animations/spring-kerning/
- `.sds-word-morph` — Word Morph: Cycles through words (loop). https://sds-motion-forge.netlify.app/animations/word-morph/
